title: Price in force on the order date: rolling join without future leakage or many-to-many notices
source_relation: adapted: point-in-time join family expressed as a function-style contract with a warnings-as-failure rule
difficulty_hypothesis: A plain join by key followed by a filter multiplies rows and raises a many-to-many warning in current dplyr; inequality and rolling joins (join_by, closest) exist only from dplyr 1.1.0; the on-or-before boundary, unmatched orders and row order are secondary traps.

mcp_relevance.rationale: join_by() with closest() and the relationship checks are version-gated dplyr features that older training material lacks; MCP could confirm the signature and the first version that offers it. A base-R solution is a complete fallback, so MCP is helpful but not necessary.
mcp_relevance.information_need: Whether and how the installed dplyr supports rolling/inequality joins and what warnings joins emit.
mcp_relevance.obtainable_without_mcp: partly: ?join_by is installed locally; base R findInterval solves it
alternative_solution_paths: inequality join then slice_max per order

calibration_risks.version_sensitivity: moderate: older dplyr idioms still work but warn

pinned_evidence.observed: left_join(orders, prices, by = 'sku') raises 'Detected an unexpected many-to-many relationship'; join_by(sku, closest(order_date >= price_date)) returns one row per order
pinned_evidence.oracle: explicit base-R scan of each sku's history; warnings are failures
